title: Navigation timing for object, embed, and multipart/x-mixed-replace documents
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

When [navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate) is [supplied with a response](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#note-navigate-called-with-response) (the `object` and `embed` processing models, and parts of a `multipart/x-mixed-replace` response after the first), the navigation params' fetch controller is null. With #12890, [create and initialize a `Document` object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#initialise-the-document-object) then creates the navigation timing entry from a fetch timing info that only has a start time. The entry reports the response's body sizes and cache state, but all network timing (`requestStart`, `responseStart`, `responseEnd`, etc.) is zero.

These documents were fetched, though. `object` and `embed` fetch the resource themselves, and multipart parts come from the original navigation fetch. We could pass the timing info through to navigate, as a fetch controller or as a fetch timing info. For `object` and `embed`, that also needs Fetch to set its controller's full timing info for those destinations. For later multipart parts, it's not obvious what the timing should be.
